data.title: Unit 3: The plant world
Classification of plants and plant cell
data.heading: Spore-bearing plants
data.text: Mosses, algae, and ferns grow in damp places and produce spores instead of seeds.
Ferns are vascular plants which produce spores on the underside of their leaves.
Spore-bearing plants release the spores in the air when they are mature.
Spores are smaller than seeds and can germinate if they fall in places where the ground is suitable for them to grow.
Spore-bearing plants produce thousands of spores.
